tone_statements.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2025. Lexique du parler banka. Mandenkan 72: 3-44. DOI 10.4000/13ewm.
tone_statements.quote: Nous avons relevé trois niveaux de tons lexicalement distinctifs en banka, notés v̀ (bas), v̄ (moyen) et v́ (haut) respectivement. A part ce constat très fondamental, le système tonal de ce parler reste à étudier. L’assignation des tons lexicaux reste préliminaire, au moins pour une partie de nos données. Dans certains cas, nous avons même dû renoncer à une notation de tons, à défaut d’une hypothèse intitiale.
tone_statements.translation: We recorded three lexically distinctive tone levels in Banka, written v̀ (low), v̄ (mid) and v́ (high) respectively. Apart from this very basic finding, the tonal system of this variety remains to be studied. The assignment of lexical tones remains preliminary, at least for part of our data. In some cases we even had to give up marking tone, for want of an initial hypothesis.
tone_statements.locator: p. 5, introduction (notes on notation and phonology, just before the lexicon)

tone_statements.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry. 2015. Clause-final negative markers in Bobo and Samogo: Parallel evolution and contact. Journal of Historical Linguistics 5(2): 235-266.
tone_statements.quote: Kastenholz (2002:97-98) reports Ban to use the CFNM má. Depending on the TAM value of the predication, this CFNM can either be the only marker of negation, as in (21), which is similar to what one finds in Jo, as in (2) above, or it co-occurs with another negative marker in the immediate post-subject slot, as in (22) and (23), which is similar to what one finds in Dzuun (cf. Section 2). Similarly to Dzuun, Ban appears to have 3 tone levels.
tone_statements.locator: section 3.2 'Ban', p. 15 of the author's prefinal
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level tones ('appears to have 3 tone levels')

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2025. Lexique du parler banka. Mandenkan 72: 3-44. DOI 10.4000/13ewm.
sources.note: Only first-hand description of Banka. Introduction (pp. 3-5) covers nasality types, velar allophones, /d/~[ɾ], the clitic =rāN, and tone: three lexically distinctive tone levels (L, M, H); 'le système tonal de ce parler reste à étudier'. No mention of stress, accent, or prominence anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/proémin: 0 hits).
